answer: An eleventh lever prices history, which can't be backdated. Standing accrues from a continuous timestamped record anchored to the public chain each epoch, so long participation is checkable against immutable anchors: you can't mint an identity today and forge it a past. A farm wanting a thousand aged identities must have actually run them that long; no shortcut. Picture an onyx bead strung each epoch: an honest strand is a relic of real time, a fake has none, and a juniper grown overnight fools no one. The attacker's cost is elapsed anchored time, which parallel hardware can't manufacture.
